issues.description: Unlike the official fix, our patch hardcodes the exclusion and does not add the DEFAULT_STRING_LOOKUPS_PROPERTY system property, so users cannot reconfigure the default lookup set without changing code. This is a feature/parity gap, not a security weakness.

pov_before_reproduced is false in the execution results, so the POV harness did not positively demonstrate the pre-patch exploit; the security conclusion rests on code analysis (script lookup removed from defaults) rather than an observed before/after trigger. regressions_ran=0 means the regression suite was not exercised in this run.

result.summary: Our patch removes the script, dns, and url lookups from the default interpolator at StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups — the exact location and defensive strategy of the official fix — thereby eliminating the code-injection (and SSRF) capability for the whole attack class rather than blocking a single payload. It is semantically equivalent to the security core of the official fix; the only divergence is that it hardcodes the exclusion instead of exposing the official's DEFAULT_STRING_LOOKUPS_PROPERTY for reconfiguration, a functionality/parity gap with no security impact. Tests were correctly updated so legitimate opt-in usage of those lookups still works. Minor caveat: the POV did not positively reproduce pre-patch and no regression tests ran, so verification leans on code analysis.
result.root_cause: StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator() wired the SCRIPT lookup (dynamic script eval) into the default lookup map, letting untrusted interpolated input reach ScriptStringLookup and execute arbitrary code; a correct fix must remove that eval-capable lookup from the default set.
